name: Saint Vitus
label: SST
lede: Too slow for Los Angeles metal, Saint Vitus found a home when Black Flag's label signed them, and the punks threw things at them anyway. They kept playing doom through new singers, a breakup and a reunion.

eras.title: Too slow for L.A. metal
eras.text: Los Angeles metal was racing toward speed and hairspray, and a band playing Black Sabbath at half speed had nowhere to go. The punks, and Greg Ginn's label, were the only people who would have them.

years.h: Tyrant forms in Los Angeles and loses its singer after one show
years.p: Guitarist [[Dave Chandler|dbcf34bc-9a5a-45ea-a586-d7c2fc64d114]], bassist [[Mark Adams|0c222999-72fa-4fb7-9205-eede45ce030d]] and drummer [[Armando Acosta|439b0bb5-df9e-4484-927f-292ce784f6cb]] start out as Tyrant. [[Scott Reagers|bb347751-07fa-4acd-925e-4b5b911caff5]] takes over from the first singer, who's gone after a single gig.
years.xp: Their touchstones were Black Sabbath, Judas Priest, Blue Cheer, Blue Öyster Cult and Alice Cooper, all played slower and heavier than the originals.

years.h: Tyrant becomes Saint Vitus, after a Black Sabbath song
years.p: The new name comes from Sabbath's St. Vitus Dance. Chandler told Louder the metal crowd wanted nothing to do with them, so they ended up in the punk scene.
years.xp: Chandler's line to Louder: "We ended up getting into the punk rock scene 'cos the metal people hated us!" It sums up the next four years.

years.h: Black Flag turn up at a Saint Vitus gig and ask them to record
years.p: SST people come to flyer the parking lot for their crossover band Overkill. Chandler asks if Black Flag will come; [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]], [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]] and [[Chuck Dukowski|19a07153-933f-4725-a5de-477cb3554517]] do, and offer a record deal that night.
years.xp:
Chandler told Westword: "Greg, Henry and Chuck showed up and they asked us that night if we wanted to record and we said, 'Hell yeah!'"

Ginn signed them, Chandler said, because they were the complete opposite of what was popular in metal.

eras.title: Thrown at the punks' feet
eras.text: SST sent a long-haired doom band on the road with Black Flag, Saccharine Trust and the rest of its hardcore roster. The crowds threw what they could find. Saint Vitus kept coming back, and the crowds changed their minds.

years.h: SST puts out Saint Vitus, a doom record on a punk label
years.p: Reagers sings, Chandler's guitar crawls, and one of the first American doom records comes out of a hardcore catalog.

years.big: Ninety percent of them hated us with a passion.
q: They threw us at the punks' feet.
yt: Live at the Embassy Hotel, Dec 20, 1984 (full show)
years.h: First cross-country tour with Black Flag
years.p: Chandler on the December 1984 tour, which ran south, up through the States, across Canada and back to L.A. The punks threw whatever wasn't nailed down.
years.xp:
SST's plan was blunt. Chandler told Louder the label simply threw Saint Vitus at the punks, and that taking the abuse and coming back is what won them over. Westword prints the rest of his answer: the crowds threw whatever wasn't nailed down and were "generally fucking with us."

The bill also carried [[The Brood|2ef8706e-baea-4c56-abec-91fbd70a303d]], [[Saccharine Trust|0bd450a7-32dd-496f-a0d4-1f71a2226add]], the Mentors, Napalm Beach and DC3.

years.h: Hallow's Victim is Reagers' last Saint Vitus album for ten years
years.p: The second SST album, with War Is Our Destiny on it, and the same year's The Walking Dead EP are the last records with Reagers until 1995.

years.big: They spit at us. We spit back.
years.h: Back on the road, the punks spit and Saint Vitus spits back
years.p: Chandler told Westword that on the August 1985 return tour the punks decided Saint Vitus were cool.

eras.title: Wino from Maryland
eras.text: The singer who defined Saint Vitus came from the D.C. suburbs: Scott "Wino" Weinrich of The Obsessed, hired after one night on tour. With him the band made Born Too Late, the record doom bands still measure themselves against.

years.h: Reagers quits, and a tape from Maryland is already in the mail
years.p: Original singer Scott Reagers leaves early in 1986. A mutual friend had sent the band a tape of the Obsessed.

years.h: [[Scott Weinrich|141b095c-a290-478e-a6ae-b1d3f7899835]], aka Wino, gets the job after one night
years.p: Saint Vitus meet the Obsessed singer on a 1986 D.C.-area tour, talk for one night, and Reagers asks him to join.
years.xp:
Chandler told Westword the band once accidentally left Wino at a highway rest stop. They missed the show, had no money, and Wino lent them twenty dollars for gas.

Wino wrote Bitter Truth, Looking Glass and Ice Monkey, which Down later covered.

years.h: Wino's first album with the band is Born Too Late
years.p: Recorded at Total Access in Redondo Beach with SST's [[Joe Carducci|6f08ef70-2da6-4575-8ec2-22438145f5d2]], it's widely called Saint Vitus' masterpiece. The title track is about being out of step with every scene around them.

years.h: Saint Vitus slow down Black Flag's Thirsty and Miserable
years.p: A thank-you to the band that got them signed: an EP led by their cover of the song.

years.h: Mournful Cries closes the SST years
years.p: The second album with Wino is the last on the label. By 1989 Saint Vitus has moved to Hellhound Records.

years.h: On Hellhound, V finds a bigger audience in Europe
years.p: The fifth Saint Vitus album, and the first on Germany's Hellhound, whose doom audience was bigger than anything the band had at home. It includes Wino's Ice Monkey.

years.h: Wino leaves to bring back the Obsessed
years.p: Hellhound releases an Obsessed retrospective, and Scott "Wino" Weinrich quits Saint Vitus to re-form his old band.

eras.title: A Swede, a hair-metal producer, a farewell
eras.text: Without Wino, Saint Vitus turned to a Swedish singer and, improbably, Don Dokken behind the board. Then Scott Reagers came home for one more album before the band called it off.

years.h: Don Dokken produces C.O.D., with a Swede out front
years.p: Former Count Raven singer Christian "Chritus" Linderson fronts Saint Vitus and tours Europe and America with them until 1993.

years.h: Scott Reagers is back for Die Healing
years.p: The original singer returns for the album Chandler considered the band's finest. After the tour, Saint Vitus breaks up in 1996.

eras.title: Kids at Wacken knew the words
eras.text: A Wacken crowd half Dave Chandler's age singing his old songs made him call the others. The classic lineup came back for one Chicago night, then for good, and lost its drummer along the way.

years.h: At Wacken, young fans know the words to Saint Vitus songs
years.p: Chandler is on stage with his band Debris Inc. when he hears the crowd sing Saint Vitus songs, and wants the others to see it.
years.xp: Chandler told Westword that young and old fans alike were singing along. He invited the other members to experience it, and Wino agreed despite his other commitments.

years.h: The Born Too Late lineup plays Chicago's Double Door
years.p: Wino, Chandler, Adams and Acosta share a stage for the first time since 1991, a one-off on July 1.

years.cap: Dave Chandler on stage with Saint Vitus, 2011
years.h: The classic lineup goes back on the road for good
years.p: Wino, Chandler, Adams and Acosta start touring again, this time without an end date.

years.h: Armando Acosta steps down, and Henry Vasquez takes the sticks
years.p: Health problems force Acosta out before the 2009 European tour ends, after 30 years. Henry Vasquez of Blood of the Sun takes over.

years.h: Armando Acosta dies at 58
years.p: Saint Vitus' drummer since 1978 died on November 25 of arterial complications, according to Wikipedia, and was buried at Riverside National Cemetery in California.

eras.title: A deportation, a return, a goodbye
eras.text: Saint Vitus' first album in seventeen years was named after the pills Dave Chandler took as a kid. Then its singer was deported, the original singer came back, and the founding bassist fell ill.

years.h: Seventeen years later, Lillie: F-65
years.p: The first studio album since 1995 and the first with Wino since 1990, on Season of Mist. The title nods to a barbiturate.
years.xp: Louder says the title refers to Chandler's childhood barbiturate addiction. It came out April 27, 2012.

q: I take full responsibility for the consequences of my actions.
years.h: Norwegian police arrest Wino with 11 grams of meth
years.p: Scott "Wino" Weinrich is arrested on November 9 for possessing methamphetamine. He's deported on November 11 and misses the tour's last six dates.
years.xp:
According to The Local, he was held three days in solitary, given a 16-day sentence, and barred from staying in Scandinavia or the EU. Saint Vitus finished the European dates without him.

Wino apologized publicly to Norway.

years.h: After 20 years, Scott Reagers is back in the band
years.p: Reagers sings a U.S. date in Austin and a European tour, then rejoins permanently.

years.h: Pat Bruders fills in for an ailing Mark Adams, then stays
years.p: On the U.S. tour with the Skull and Witch Mountain, Pat Bruders of [[Crowbar|04fc15f9-2555-4699-9215-2ee6c84a2346]] and Down plays bass because Adams has health problems.

years.h: A second self-titled album, 35 years after the first
years.p: Saint Vitus (2019) is the ninth studio album, with Reagers, Chandler, Bruders and Vasquez.

years.h: Mark Adams dies at 64
years.p: The founding bassist, off the road since 2016 and revealed in 2018 to have Parkinson's disease, died of complications from it on May 23. He played on every Saint Vitus album until 2012.
